Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.

Which word belongs to this topic?
Core Active Vocabulary (7 items):

kitchen — the room where you cook. Example: The kitchen is small but bright.
bedroom — the room where you sleep. Example: There are two bedrooms.
bathroom — the room with a bath or shower. Example: The bathroom is next to the bedroom.
living room — the room where you relax. Example: We watch TV in the living room.
office — a room where people work. Example: My office is on the first floor.
balcony — a small outdoor floor on a building. Example: There is a balcony with a view.
garden — an area with grass and plants by a house. Example: The garden is small but green.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• There is a ...
• There are two ...
• How many rooms are there?
• The kitchen is next to ...
• Is there a balcony?
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.

Complete the sentence with a word from the list.

LIVING room, BEDroom
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word carries the main stress?
Grammar focus: There is / There are.
Use there is for one room and there are for several: There is a kitchen. There are two bedrooms. Ask: How many rooms are there?
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
Choose the correct sentence.
___ two bedrooms in my flat.
Complete the sentence.
Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
My flat has got two bedrooms, a kitchen and a living room. There is a small balcony and there is no garden. The bathroom is next to the bedroom.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: How many rooms are there? B: There are four: a kitchen, a living room and two bedrooms. A: Is there a balcony? B: Yes, there is.
Speaking: pair work

• There is a ...
• There are two ...
• How many rooms are there?
Writing: short text
